drafts.opening: We are building DESIGN:OS Studio so a designer can finish a reviewed handoff, not just generate a screen.
drafts.body:
We are building DESIGN:OS Studio so a designer can finish a reviewed handoff, not just generate a screen.

**v0.6.0 — AI Design**

Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Grok and Antigravity can run as sessions; edits can be reviewed with Keep or Revert; each turn records duration, tools and changed layers.

What I would actually try:
• Open a real design file locally → review the same canvas without a cloud handoff.
• Ask an agent for one bounded change → see the proposed result before accepting it.
• Inspect the changed layers → keep the useful turn or revert it.
• Check the implementation view → leave engineering a concrete starting point.
• Capture the screen → compare the result with the expected design.
• Save the working file → keep the decision history with the project.

**From “AI generates a screen” to “an agent works inside a design environment with state, review and evidence.”**

Free, open source. We are sharing the build in public and want practical feedback from people doing this work.

https://github.com/jangtrinh/design-os-studio
https://github.com/jangtrinh/design-os-studio/releases/tag/v0.6.0

What would you test first: **accuracy, controllability hay speed?**?
